deep.reconstruction:
Setting, read from the neighbouring pages. There is a 'symmetric' simplicial-type object. Each X_n carries an action of the symmetric group S_n and can be thought of as tuples of n vertices.
- X_1 = {e_1} is a point.
- X_2 (edges) carries an involution σ, (x,y) ↦ (y,x), and a degenerate element e_2.
- X_3 (triangles) carries an S_3-action, with ρ the cyclic permutation (x,y,z) ↦ (y,z,x).
- The degeneracy is d = δ_1 : X_2 → X_3, (x,y) ↦ (x,y,y), and the face is p : X_3 → X_2, (x,y,z) ↦ (x,y).
- X_3' is the S_3-subset generated by d(X_2). Previous page: X_3' = {e_3} ⊔ (S_3 ∧_{(1,σ_1)} X_2*), with X_2* = X_2 \ {e_2}.
- The map (p, pρ) : X_3 → X_2 × X_2 sends a triangle to two composable edges. The previous page requires it to be surjective (épi). This is an inner-horn (Λ^2_1) filling / composition condition: any two composable edges bound a triangle.

What this page does.
1. It computes the image of X_3' under (p, pρ):
- e_3 ↦ (e_2, e_2).
- For ξ ∈ X_2*: dξ ↦ (ξ, e_2), ρdξ ↦ (e_2, σξ), ρ²dξ ↦ (σξ, ξ).
- The image is therefore Σ = Σ_1 ∪ Σ_2 ∪ Δ', where Σ_1 = X_2 × {e_2}, Σ_2 = {e_2} × X_2, and Δ' is the image of the twisted diagonal δ' = (σ, id).
- The three pieces meet pairwise exactly in (e_2, e_2).
2. It asks when Σ = X_2 × X_2, i.e. when the triangles coming from degeneracies alone already satisfy the filling condition.
- The complement of Σ_1 ∪ Σ_2 is X_2* × X_2*. One needs X_2* × X_2* ⊂ Δ', i.e. η = σξ for all ξ, η ∈ X_2*.
- This forces |X_2*| ≤ 1. Either X_2 = {e_2}, or X_2 = {e_2, ξ} with σ acting trivially.
- If |X_2*| ≥ 2: with one σ-orbit of size ≥ 2, (ξ, ξ) ∉ Δ'; with ≥ 2 orbits, take ξ, η in different orbits.
3. Next page: with X_2 of cardinality 2 and X_3 = X_3' (four triangles), he tests whether certain squares of faces and degeneracies are cartesian. These are Segal/coskeletality-type conditions.

Modern reading. The case X_2 = {e, ξ} with four triangles is exactly the 3-truncated nerve of the group Z/2, viewed as a symmetric simplicial set. The page is a small classification lemma inside an exploration of symmetric simplicial sets with a single vertex (or of a combinatorial model for strata).
errors: No substantive mathematical error; the computations of (p,pρ) on ρ^i dξ are correct under the stated conventions.

Minor imprecision: the necessary condition is phrased as surjectivity of 'X_2* → X_2*×X_2*'. What is meant is surjectivity of δ' restricted to X_2* onto X_2*×X_2*, which uses σ(X_2*) ⊂ X_2*. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Image of degenerate-generated triangles under the 'two composable edges' map (p, pρ): the union of the two axes and the twisted diagonal (σ, id)
ideas.modern_name: Horn-filling/Segal map X_3 → X_2 ×_{X_1} X_2 for symmetric simplicial sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard simplicial combinatorics; symmetric simplicial sets studied by Grandis and others
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses related simplicial/Kan conditions, but not this computation

ideas.what: Degenerate triangles alone fill all horns only if |X_2| ≤ 2 with trivial σ, i.e. the trivial group or Z/2 as a one-object structure
ideas.modern_name: Elementary classification; nerve of Z/2 as a symmetric simplicial set

deep.surprise_reason: A routine combinatorial check within an exploratory computation on symmetric simplicial-type objects. It is correct but elementary, and it identifies nothing beyond the nerve of Z/2 or the point.
transcription_corrections: The circled symbol at the top is the page number '(6)' (previous page 5, next page (7)), not '(σ)'.
'ou Δ' est l'image' should read 'où Δ' est l'image'.
'dont l'intersection des deux par deux sont toutes égales' reads more naturally as 'dont les intersections deux à deux sont toutes égales à {(e_2,e_2)}'.
In the bracketed argument, the struck word is likely 'deux', followed by 'au moins deux orbites'; the transcription is essentially right.
